references.text: God describes himself as the one who leads and gathers his sheep, in contrast to the evil shepherds who scatter them, which is the direct contextual theme of Jesus' teaching on the proper entrance to the sheepfold.
The prophecy that the Lord himself will stand as shepherd for his people, an image Jesus later applies to himself as the one who enters through the door to save and gather the sheep.
The psalm describes the Lord as a shepherd who leads his people to safe places, an image that Jesus expands by defining the right way into the sheepfold as safety from thieves and robbers.
Jesus' own explanation immediately following the verse, where he makes clear that he himself is the door, and that whoever enters through him will be saved, which is the theological core of verse 1.
The contrast between the good shepherd and the hired hand who flees underscores the theme of the false entrance and the dangerous behavior of those who lack authority to lead the sheepfold.
